name: LTC2309CF#PBF
title: 8-channel, 12-bit, 14ksps SAR ADC with I²C interface
summary: A 12-bit successive-approximation converter with an eight-input mux, a 2.5V bandgap reference buffered to 4.096V, an internal conversion clock and a slave-only I²C port with nine pin-set addresses plus a global one. It runs from one 5V supply at up to 14ksps, drawing 2.3mA converting, 210µA napping and 7µA asleep. Inputs are software-selected as single-ended or differential, unipolar or bipolar. Packages are a 24-lead 4mm × 4mm QFN and a 20-lead TSSOP.

circuits.title: Basic connection
circuits.description: The converter on a 5 V rail with its three decoupling points populated: VDD carries 0.1 µF and 10 µF, VREF carries 2.2 µF and REFCOMP carries 0.1 µF and 10 µF, each to ground. The eight channels and COM are analog inputs, taking 0 V to 4.096 V unipolar or ±2.048 V bipolar; AD0, AD1, SCL and SDA go to the system.

circuits.title: Optional RC input filtering for a single-ended input
circuits.description: A 50 Ω series resistor and a 2000 pF capacitor to ground form a low-pass in front of CH0, holding the input bandwidth to 1.6 MHz. COM is grounded for single-ended unipolar measurement and REFCOMP keeps its 0.1 µF and 10 µF decoupling.
notes: NPO or silver-mica capacitors and metal-film resistors keep the filter from adding distortion.

circuits.title: Optional RC input filtering for differential inputs
circuits.description: Each leg of a differential pair passes through 50 Ω into CH0 or CH1. A 1000 pF capacitor sits from each input pin to ground and a third 1000 pF sits across the pair, filtering both common-mode and differential noise. REFCOMP is decoupled with 0.1 µF and 10 µF.

circuits.title: LT1790A-2.5 as an external reference
circuits.description: An LT1790A-2.5 running from 5 V drives the VREF pin directly, overriding the internal 2.5 V bandgap through its 8 kΩ series resistor for better accuracy or lower drift. VREF keeps its 2.2 µF capacitor; the internal amplifier still makes 4.096 V at REFCOMP, decoupled by 10 µF and 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: Overdriving REFCOMP with the LT1790A-4.096
circuits.description: VREF is tied to ground, which turns off the internal reference buffer, and an LT1790A-4.096 from 5 V supplies REFCOMP directly with 10 µF and 0.1 µF across it. REFCOMP may be driven anywhere from 1 V to VDD this way.

circuits.title: Driving the LTC2309 with ±10V input signals using a precision attenuator
circuits.description: An LT1991 precision difference amplifier on ±10 V rails, its on-chip resistor network wired as an attenuator, scales a ±10 V signal into the converter's input range. An LT1790-2.5 from 5 V (0.1 µF in, 1 µF out) drives network pins 3 and 10; network pin 8 returns from the amplifier output, and pins 2 and 9 stay open. The output reaches CH0 through 100 Ω with 47 pF to ground; COM, AD0 and AD1 are grounded. VDD takes 10 µF and 0.1 µF, VREF 2.2 µF, REFCOMP 0.1 µF and 10 µF, and SCL and SDA run to the control logic with 1.7 kΩ pull-ups to 5 V.
notes: LT1991 network pins: 1 and 10 reach the amplifier inputs through 450 kΩ, 2 and 9 through 150 kΩ, 3 and 8 through 50 kΩ; 450 kΩ with 4 pF sits from the inverting input to the output and from the non-inverting input to pin 5.

equations.name: Equivalent input resistance with a large filter capacitor
equations.note: With a large CFILTER (1µF for instance) the switched input averages into this resistance in series with a VREFCOMP/2 source.

operation.text: A 12-bit SAR converter built on a capacitive charge-redistribution DAC. The sampled input is compared, MSB first, against binary-weighted charges by a differential comparator; at the end the 12-bit word is moved into output latches for the I²C port. Both the + and – mux outputs are sampled at the same moment, so signals common to both are rejected by the fully differential sample-and-hold. An internal trimmed clock gives a 1.3µs typical, 1.8µs worst-case conversion.

S/D, O/S, S1 and S0 in the DIN word select the input: any of CH0-CH7 single-ended against COM, or the pairs CH0/CH1, CH2/CH3, CH4/CH5, CH6/CH7 differentially in either polarity. Single-ended and differential use can be mixed, and the selection can change between one conversion and the next. For unipolar single-ended work COM is grounded; for bipolar it sits at REFCOMP/2, midway between GND and REFCOMP, and it must be quiet.

UNI selects the range. Unipolar: 0 to REFCOMP (0V to 4.096V with the internal reference), output in straight binary. Bipolar: ±REFCOMP/2 (±2.048V), output in two's complement. With FS = 4.096V one LSB is 1mV. Each input itself must stay between –0.05V and REFCOMP.

Each input looks like 55pF (CIN) behind about 100Ω (RON), switched onto the selected channel once per conversion; between samples only leakage flows. A low-impedance source can drive the pins directly; a higher one needs more acquisition time. Any RC filter must let the input settle to 12 bits within tACQ when DC accuracy matters. A single-pole RC is often enough to keep source noise out.

A trimmed, temperature-compensated 2.5V bandgap appears at VREF through an 8kΩ series resistor; VREF needs at least 2.2µF of ceramic decoupling. An amplifier multiplies it up to 4.096V at REFCOMP, which needs 10µF and 0.1µF ceramics in parallel for stability and noise. An external 2.5V reference may drive VREF directly. Grounding VREF shuts off the buffer so REFCOMP can be driven from outside, anywhere from 1V to VDD.

The part is a slave only: SCL is always an input and SDA is open-drain, needing a pull-up to VDD. Standard (100kbit/s) and fast (400kbit/s) modes are supported. VDD should stay powered while the bus is active, otherwise the ESD diodes load the bus lines. Two registers exist: a 6-bit input register (the DIN word) and a 12-bit output register holding the last result.

AD0 and AD1 each read as low, high or floating, giving nine addresses (Table 2). A float needs under 10pF on the pin and more than 2MΩ to either rail; high or low needs 10kΩ or less. A global address, 1101011, is also recognised for synchronising several converters.

A conversion begins at a STOP issued after the part has been addressed for a read or a write. While converting the part NACKs any access; once done it ACKs. A STOP between the 8th SCL of the address frame and the end of the read/write also starts a conversion, though its result may be wrong for lack of acquisition time. There is no pipeline latency: the result read belongs to the conversion just finished.

After an address with R/W = 0 the part ACKs and takes one byte: the six DIN bits (S/D first, SLP sixth), latched on rising SCL, then two ignored bits. At power-up an internal reset clears all DIN bits to 0.

After an address with R/W = 1 the part ACKs and sends up to two bytes, changing SDA on falling SCL so the master can latch on rising edges: B11 (MSB) to B0, then four zeros. A STOP after the two bytes starts the next conversion.

When the channel never changes, reads can follow one another without writes, the DIN word staying as last written (or at its power-up zeros). Alternatively, after a conversion, a write, a repeated START and a read can be chained, closing with a STOP that launches a conversion with the new settings.

With every converter on the bus finished, the master sends START, the global address 1101011 with a write, an optional DIN byte and STOP: all converters (including other I²C SAR ADCs of the family) start converting together, with new channel settings if a byte was sent. Global reads are refused with a NACK.

On a read, acquisition starts at the rising edge of the 9th SCL after the address frame; on a write, at the falling edge of the 6th clock after the DIN word, using the newly programmed channel. At least 240ns of acquisition is needed before a conversion begins.

After each conversion the part drops automatically into nap (SLP = 0) or sleep (SLP = 1). In nap only the reference and REFCOMP buffer stay on and the supply falls to 210µA, so average power scales with rate: 300µA at 1ksps. In sleep the draw is 7µA as long as the digital inputs are quiet. Addressing the part wakes it; from sleep the reference needs tREFWAKE = 200ms to recharge the 2.2µF and 10µF capacitors before a conversion should start.

Use a board with a solid ground plane; all GND pins and the QFN exposed pad go to it. Keep digital and analog traces apart, never routing a digital line beside an analog one, and guard analog inputs with ground. Decouple VREF, REFCOMP and VDD to the plane right at the pins, with wide, low-impedance returns. VDD takes 10µF plus a 0.1µF ceramic at each VDD pin (three on QFN, two on TSSOP).
